findings.title: Atomic report write leaks its temp file when the write fails
findings.description: `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` is created, then `handle.write(text)` runs inside the `with`. If `write` or `replace` raises `OSError`, for example with a full disk, the `.{name}.*` temp file stays in the runs dir. The handler logs and re-raises but never unlinks it. The report is rewritten after every item, so repeated failures leave a growing set of hidden files. There is also no flush or fsync before the rename, so the "never sees a partial file" claim only holds against concurrent readers, not against a crash. Unlink the temp file in the `except` branch, using `contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError)` with a justifying comment.

findings.title: CLI item-resume module imports private helpers from `run.py` through a circular import
findings.description: `run_item.py` imports `_apply_param_overrides` and `_run_pipeline_sdk` inside the function body. It needs `# pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]` and a comment saying "run.py imports this module". That is a layering inversion: the extracted module depends on private internals of its caller. Move the shared helpers into a third module that both import, or have `run.py` pass the pipeline runner and the override parser in as parameters. Passing them in also removes the need for the pyright suppressions.

findings.title: Run-lock decision depends on a `definition` whose source in the resume paths I could not confirm
findings.description: The `--resume` and implicit-resume branches call `_locked(definition, ...)`, but the diff shows no change that loads the definition for the resumed pipeline. If `definition` comes from the CLI `pipeline` argument or from an earlier load, a resumed run whose `state.pipeline` is mutating could skip the lock. Alternatively, the call could pick up the wrong pipeline's answer. The test `test_a_plain_resume_of_a_paused_run_with_the_lock_held_exits_2` mocks `state.pipeline = "P6"`, so it does not distinguish the two cases. I did not confirm where `definition` is bound, so please verify it is `load_pipeline(state.pipeline)` and add a test where the CLI argument and the state pipeline differ.

findings.title: Dead and duplicated control flow in the lock and resume paths
findings.description: `raise AssertionError("unreachable")` follows a `with` block whose body always returns. It is dead code and needs `# pragma: no cover`. `_locked` and `_take_run_lock` in `run.py` also split one concern in two. `_locked` catches `typer.Exit` only to close the coroutine, which is a workaround for creating the coroutine before the lock is taken. Take the lock first and build the coroutine inside the `with`, or pass a factory (a zero-argument callable that returns the coroutine). That removes the close-and-reraise step.

findings.title: `ItemRerun.replace` can fail with a bare `StopIteration`
findings.description: `next(i for i, r in enumerate(records) if r.index == record.index)` has no default. If the record index is not in the loaded report, `StopIteration` is raised. Inside a coroutine this becomes `RuntimeError("coroutine raised StopIteration")`, and `resume_item` does not catch it, so the failure is neither handled nor clearly reported. `_reconcile` and `_outcome` use the same pattern. Raise an explicit error that names the index.

findings.title: Style and typing hygiene
findings.description: Several new lines are well over 88 characters, including the `_write_each_report` signature and `_add_record`, along with the `_step_mutates` line in `run_lock.py` and `_not_ready_reason` in `sources.py`. The project rules call for 88. The new tests also use many `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments and untyped helpers such as `body_runner`, `resume` and `_record`. This conflicts with the strict-pyright rule. Run `ruff format` and type the helpers, for example with a small `Protocol` or a typed `ResumeOutcome` return.

findings.title: Reserved-param, schema-version and run-lock design is sound
findings.description: The reserved keys are defined once and enforced at three entry points: `-p`, the pipeline `params` block, and stored run state. `report.json` carries a schema version and fails explicitly on a mismatch. The run lock never waits, is released by the OS when its holder dies, and is covered by tests for the held, killed-holder, unopenable-file and separate-worktree cases. Halt, flag-kind and exhaustion paths each have a test that asserts the observable signal. Aside from the two items above that I could not fully verify, the new I/O paths log at ERROR or WARNING and do not swallow exceptions.

structured_findings.summary: Atomic report write leaks its temp file when the write fails
CLI item-resume module imports private helpers from `run.py` through a circular import
Run-lock decision depends on a `definition` whose source in the resume paths I could not confirm
Dead and duplicated control flow in the lock and resume paths
Reserved-param, schema-version and run-lock design is sound
